purpose: Fifth Benchmark v2 case, Epic 4.3 Bucket C, highest evidence bar: a real, DOI-verified pair of peer-reviewed papers reaching opposing conclusions on the same specific structural-neuroimaging question in autism, plus a third real source (a meta-analysis) that itself characterizes this as a genuine, literature-documented inconsistency. Tests whether pipeline/gap_challenger.py's decision table correctly resolves to CONTESTED (contradiction_count >= 1) rather than converging to LIKELY_CLOSED/CLOSED (which would mean the judge failed to recognize that relevant papers disagree) or defaulting to OPEN (which would mean the search funnel failed to surface this well-known, heavily-cited literature at all).
ground_truth_note: Acceptable terminal status for this case: CONTESTED only. This is a deliberately constructed real contradictory pair, so CONTESTED is the only status that correctly reflects it. LIKELY_CLOSED or CLOSED would be a serious miss (treating opposing volumetric findings as converging agreement). OPEN would be a miss (failing to find substantial, well-cited existing structural MRI literature on this exact question). PARTIALLY_OPEN would indicate the search found the relevant papers but the LLM judge failed to recognize that they contradict each other -- a real, if softer, miss worth flagging via challenge_funnel.judged_candidates. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is an acceptable, honest non-failure if search coverage genuinely fell below threshold that run.

gap.title: Direction of amygdala volume alteration in autism spectrum disorder
gap.description: Whether amygdala volume in individuals with autism spectrum disorder is enlarged or reduced relative to neurotypical controls has not been established -- independent structural MRI studies report opposing directions of volumetric difference for the same structure.
gap.missing_connection: consistent direction of amygdala volume alteration in autism spectrum disorder across development

verification.method: Real web search, 2026-08-24 -- not assumed, not generated by the pipeline under test.
verification.summary: Two real, DOI-verified structural MRI studies report opposite directions of amygdala volume difference in autism, and a real meta-analysis explicitly cites both while characterizing amygdala volume findings across ages as inconsistent. Sparks et al. (2002, Neurology) measured 45 children with ASD aged 3-4 and found bilateral amygdala ENLARGEMENT relative to typically-developing and developmentally-delayed controls, with enlargement in a strictly-defined-autism subgroup exceeding the overall increase in cerebral volume. Nacewicz et al. (2006, Archives of General Psychiatry) measured 28 adolescent/adult males with autism and found SMALLER amygdala volume was associated with greater nonverbal social impairment (slower emotional-expression discrimination, less eye fixation) -- the opposite direction of volumetric difference in an older cohort. Nickl-Jockschat et al.'s meta-analysis of VBM studies (2011/2012, Human Brain Mapping) explicitly cites both directions -- 'a preferential overgrowth of the frontal and the temporal lobes in particular as well as the amygdala in 2- to 4-year-old ASD patients [Sparks et al., 2002]' versus 'most volumetric studies on adolescent and adult ASD patients report...reduced volume...of the amygdala [Nacewicz et al., 2006...]' -- and states that a meta-analysis on volumetric studies showed 'no consistent changes of the amygdalae... over all ages,' i.e. a real reviewer characterizing this specific question as an established inconsistency, not merely under-researched.

sources.title: Brain structural abnormalities in young children with autism spectrum disorder (Sparks et al., Neurology, 2002)
Amygdala Volume and Nonverbal Social Impairment in Adolescent and Adult Males With Autism (Nacewicz et al., Archives of General Psychiatry, 2006)

Brain structure anomalies in autism spectrum disorder -- a meta-analysis of VBM studies using anatomic likelihood estimation (Nickl-Jockschat et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2011/2012) -- explicitly cites both opposing findings and reports no consistent amygdala volume change across ages

known_contradicting_pair.title: Brain structural abnormalities in young children with autism spectrum disorder
known_contradicting_pair.finding: Bilateral amygdala ENLARGEMENT in 3-4 year old children with ASD relative to typically-developing and developmentally-delayed controls; in a subgroup with strictly-defined autism, amygdala enlargement exceeded the overall increase in cerebral volume.

known_contradicting_pair.title: Amygdala Volume and Nonverbal Social Impairment in Adolescent and Adult Males With Autism
known_contradicting_pair.finding: SMALLER (reduced) amygdala volume in adolescent/adult males with autism was associated with greater nonverbal social impairment -- the opposite direction of volumetric difference from Sparks et al. 2002's early-childhood finding.

notes: Both DOIs independently confirmed to resolve via Europe PMC metadata lookup (title/authors/journal/year match) in addition to publisher pages, so the pair is not just plausible-sounding but individually machine-verifiable. The amygdala developmental-trajectory literature (early overgrowth, later reduction) is a well-known, heavily-cited case in autism neuroimaging, which is why it was chosen over a less-established candidate controversy.
